citation: Chaurasia N, Ram M, Verma P, Mehta N, Bharot N. A federated learning approach to network intrusion detection using residual networks in industrial IoT networks. The Journal of Supercomputing 80(13):18325-18346, 2024. doi:10.1007/s11227-024-06153-2

A1.evidence: Abstract/Experiments: 'X-IIoTID ... with an 80–20 training–testing split' — how the split was made (random, stratified, temporal) is not stated; X-IIoTID has no official train/test files.

A2.evidence: Proposed ResNet on per-record features; no windows, sequences or time steps described in methodology.

A3.evidence: No normalization/scaling/encoding described in the methodology or experimental sections.

A4.evidence: 'each client performing four epochs of local training in each communication round. The FL process encompasses 20 communication rounds.'

A5.evidence: Federated setting stated once for the federated environment ('The dataset is distributed among 10 clients ... four epochs ... 20 communication rounds') under which all FL models are compared; centralized: 'In DL methods, we used batch size = 32, and the number of epochs = 32.'

A6.evidence: Table 3 ('Comparison of various classification techniques in centralized environment') and Fig. 7/9 federated comparisons are authors' own runs; Table 1 related work lists methods only, no copied numbers.

A7.evidence: Metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall (TPR), TNR, F1, F2; no MCC/balanced accuracy/G-mean.

A8.evidence: 'These training data are distributed among 10 clients while maintaining equal distribution for each client.'

A9.evidence: No repeated runs, means, standard deviations or seeds reported.

A10.evidence: Only X-IIoTID used; no cross-dataset evaluation.

A11.evidence: No code link; Data availability: 'Not applicable.'

notes: Springer page read via web extraction. A5 borderline: the federated budget is stated as a single environment setting rather than explicitly 'for all methods'; coded same because it describes the shared federated environment for all compared FL models — flag for second coder. Binary task (attack vs normal) on a roughly balanced dataset (421,417 normal vs 399,417 attack).
